content: 1. Avoid any contact of Mupirocin with the eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water. 2. If a patient experiences sensitization or severe local irritation while using Bactroban Cream, the treatment should be discontinued immediately. An alternative therapy appropriate for the infection should be initiated. 3. Prolonged use of Bactroban Cream, like other antibacterial agents, may lead to the overgrowth of non-susceptible microorganisms, including fungi. 4. Bactroban Cream is not designed for application on mucosal surfaces. 5. Patients should use this medication strictly as directed by their healthcare provider. It is intended for external use only. 6. Avoid applying the cream near or in the eyes. 7. If desired, the treated area may be covered with a gauze dressing. 8. Patients should report any signs of local adverse reactions to their healthcare provider. If irritation, severe itching, or rash occurs, the medication should be stopped, and the healthcare provider should be contacted. 9. If no improvement is observed within 3 to 5 days of use, patients should consult their healthcare provider. 10. The effects of using topical Mupirocin Calcium Cream concurrently with other topical products have not been studied. 11. Long-term studies in animals to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of Mupirocin Calcium have not been conducted. 12. Studies performed with Mupirocin Calcium or Mupirocin Sodium in vitro and in vivo, including tests such as rat primary hepatocyte unscheduled DNA synthesis, DNA strand break analysis, Ames test, E. coli mutation assay, human lymphocyte metaphase analysis, mouse lymphoma assay, and bone marrow micronuclei assay in mice, did not indicate any mutagenic potential. 13. Fertility studies in rats, with Mupirocin administered subcutaneously at doses up to 49 times the human topical dose of 1 gram/day (approximately 20 mg Mupirocin per day) on a mg/m² basis, showed no evidence of impaired fertility due to Mupirocin Sodium. 14. Mupirocin is classified as Pregnancy Category B. Teratology studies in rats and rabbits, with subcutaneous administration of Mupirocin at doses up to 78 and 154 times the human topical dose of 1 gram/day (approximately 20 mg Mupirocin per day) on a mg/m² basis, revealed no evidence of harm to the fetus. However, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. This drug should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, as animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response. 15. It is unknown whether Mupirocin is excreted in human milk. Since many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when Bactroban Cream is administered to a nursing woman. 16. The safety and effectiveness of Bactroban Cream have been established in pediatric patients aged 3 months to 16 years. This is supported by evidence from adequate and well-controlled studies in adults, along with additional data from 93 pediatric patients included in pivotal trials. 17. In two well-controlled studies, 30 patients older than 65 years were treated with Bactroban Cream. No overall differences in efficacy or safety were observed in this population compared to younger patients.
